Title: Product Design and Manufacturing Glossary

Reference page

By [Andrew Hunter](https://oriondesign.xyz/about/), Product Design Engineer · Last reviewed 27 November 2026 · 350 terms

# Product design and manufacturing glossary.

Plain-English definitions of the terms you will meet when developing, making and selling a physical product: from prototypes and tooling
to landed cost, funding and certification. Where a term is explained in more depth on Orion Design, follow the link.

## A

ABS

Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene: a common, low-cost rigid plastic with a good surface finish, widely used for enclosures and consumer products. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

Acceptable quality limit (AQL)

The defect level used with a sampling standard such as ISO 2859-1 to decide whether a production batch passes inspection. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/quality-control-and-first-article-inspection.html)

Acetal (POM)

Polyoxymethylene: a stiff, low-friction engineering plastic used for gears, clips and mechanisms. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

Aluminium tool

An injection-mould tool machined from aluminium: quicker and cheaper to make than steel, but it wears sooner, so it suits prototypes and lower volumes. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Amortisation

Spreading a one-off cost, such as tooling, across the units it helps produce, so it can be included in the unit cost. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/manufacturing-and-cost.html)

Angel investor

An individual who invests their own money in an early-stage company, usually in exchange for shares. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

Anisotropy

Having different properties in different directions. A 3D-printed part, especially one printed by FDM, is often weaker between its layers than along them. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-a-3d-printing-process.html)

Anodising

A process that grows a hard oxide layer out of the surface of a metal, usually aluminium. It can be clear or dyed, resists wear and corrosion, does not chip like paint and is electrically insulating. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Assembly time

The labour time needed to put a product together, which drives assembly cost on every unit. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/assembly-time.html)

## B

Batch production

Making a product in discrete quantities rather than continuously, typical for start-ups and lower-volume products.

Bead blasting

Firing fine glass beads or similar media at a part to give an even matt texture that hides machining marks, often before anodising. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Bending stress

The stress in a part as it bends, highest at the surface furthest from the middle of the section and where the bending moment is largest, such as the root of a cantilever bracket. Compared with the material's yield or allowable stress, it shows whether the part will spring back or take a permanent bend. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/bracket-deflection-calculator.html)

Bill of materials (BOM)

The structured list of every part, material and quantity needed to make a product, used for costing, purchasing and assembly. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-estimate-manufacturing-cost.html)

Billet

A cylinder of aluminium, heated until it is soft but still solid, that a press pushes through the die to make an extrusion. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/aluminium-extrusions-for-product-enclosures.html)

Board-to-board connector

A connector that joins two circuit boards directly, stacked or at right angles, so they need no cable and locate each other. The housing must still hold both boards so the connector does not carry the load. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cables-wiring-and-connectors-inside-a-product.html)

Boss

A raised cylindrical feature on a moulded part that receives a screw, pin or insert. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Brand registry

A programme run by some large online marketplaces that helps brand owners manage their listings and report copies. Such programmes generally require a trade mark, registered or applied for, in the relevant country. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/trade-marks-and-product-names.html)

Brazing

Joining metal parts with a filler metal that melts at a lower temperature than the parts themselves. It distorts parts less than welding and can join different metals, but is permanent. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html)

Break-even point

The sales volume at which total contribution covers fixed costs, so the product neither makes nor loses money. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/break-even-calculator.html)

Bridge tooling

Lower-cost, faster tooling used to make early production parts while demand and design settle, before committing to full production tooling. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/risk-progressive-manufacturing-strategy.html)

Buffer stock

Extra stock of a part or product held in reserve, so a late delivery or a sudden rise in demand does not stop production or sales. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/planning-a-pilot-production-run.html)

Burn rate

How quickly a business spends its cash each month before it is profitable. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/cashflow-projection.html)

Business case

A structured argument that a product is worth developing, bringing together market, price, cost, investment and risk. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/building-a-hardware-business-case.html)

## C

Cable gland

A fitting that clamps a seal around a cable where it passes through the wall of a housing, so water and dust cannot follow the cable in. It suits round cables of a known diameter. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

CAD

Computer-aided design: software used to create the 3D models and drawings that define a product.

Cantilever snap fit

The most common type of snap fit: a hook on the end of a short flexible beam that bends as the parts are pushed together and springs back behind a catch. The strain at the root of the beam must stay below the material's permissible strain. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/snap-fit-calculator.html)

Capacitive touch

A touch control with no moving parts that works through a solid wall, so it seals well and has nothing to wear. It needs light, sound or vibration as feedback, and gloves or water can stop it working reliably. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-buttons-switches-and-controls.html)

Carbon footprint

The greenhouse gas emissions linked to a product across the life cycle stages counted, usually expressed as carbon dioxide equivalent. It measures one impact, where a life cycle assessment looks at many. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-carbon-footprint-vs-lca.html)

Case quantity

The number of units packed in each outer case, often chosen to suit how a retailer orders. Changing it changes the case size and how cases fit on a pallet. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-ready-packaging-and-barcodes.html)

Cash flow

The movement of money into and out of a business over time. A profitable business can still run short of cash if money goes out before it comes in. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/calculating-hardware-startup-cash-flow.html)

Cash low point

The lowest point of a business's cumulative cash forecast, which sets the minimum funding it needs. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

Cavity

The hollow in an injection-mould tool that forms the part. A multi-cavity tool makes several parts per cycle. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

CE marking

The conformity marking used for many products sold in the EU and in Northern Ireland, and recognised in Great Britain for many product types. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Change control

A simple, recorded process for approving design changes once a design is frozen, because changes then affect tools, suppliers and test reports. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/development-and-prototyping.html)

Channel margin

The share of the retail price kept by a retailer, distributor or marketplace. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/route-to-market-and-margins.html)

Classes of goods and services

The groups into which goods and services are divided when a trade mark is registered. A registration covers particular goods and services, so the same word can be registered by different owners for unrelated goods. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/trade-marks-and-product-names.html)

Clearance fit

A fit in which the shaft is always smaller than the hole, so there is always a gap. Used for parts that must slide, turn or assemble by hand. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/tolerances-and-engineering-drawings.html)

Clinching

Joining overlapping metal sheets by pressing them into an interlocking button, with no heat, fasteners or consumables. The joint is permanent. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html)

CNC machining

Computer-controlled cutting of parts from solid material, used for prototypes, precise parts and low volumes. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/manufacturing-and-cost.html)

COGS

Cost of goods sold: the direct cost of making and delivering each unit sold. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/product-cost-estimator.html)

Cold-chamber machine

A die-casting machine in which metal is ladled from a separate furnace into a shot sleeve, then a plunger drives it into the die. It is used for aluminium, which would attack parts left sitting in it, and for much magnesium. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/die-casting-explained.html)

Colour, material and finish (CMF)

The visible colours, materials, textures and surface finishes chosen for a product, and how they look, feel and age. CMF is usually led by industrial design. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/industrial-design-vs-engineering-design.html)

Commodity code

The classification number that sets the duty rate and import rules for a product. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/landed-cost-freight-duty-vat.html)

Concept selection

Choosing between design concepts using structured criteria rather than preference. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-engineers-choose-between-concepts.html)

Conformal coating

A thin protective film applied over an assembled circuit board to help it resist moisture and condensation. It is lighter and less permanent than potting. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

Conformity assessment

The process of showing a product meets the regulations that apply to it, by self-assessment or through an independent body. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Contingency

Money set aside in a budget for problems that will happen but cannot yet be named; commonly 15 to 25 per cent in hardware development. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/estimating-hardware-development-costs.html)

Contract manufacturer

A company that sources parts, assembles, tests and packs a product to the customer's design. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html)

Contribution

Selling price received minus the variable costs of each sale: the amount each unit contributes to fixed costs and profit. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/break-even-calculator.html)

Copyright

Automatic protection for original works such as drawings, manuals, software and photographs. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/ip-partners-and-compliance.html)

Core

The part of an injection-mould tool that forms the inside surfaces of a moulded part. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Coring out

Hollowing a thick feature of a moulded part so it is made of walls close to the nominal wall thickness. It avoids sink marks and voids, and shortens cooling time. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/from-3d-printed-prototype-to-moulded-part.html)

Cosmetic face

A face of a part that people will see or touch, marked on the drawing so that suppliers keep marks, defects and support or contact points off it and finish it to the agreed standard. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Cost-down

Lowering the cost of making a product that is already in production, for example by removing parts, operations or unneeded precision. Each change needs validating before it reaches production. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/reducing-the-cost-of-an-existing-product.html)

Cradle to gate

A footprint boundary covering raw materials and manufacturing, up to the product leaving the factory. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-carbon-footprint-vs-lca.html)

Cradle to grave

A footprint boundary covering a product's whole life: materials, manufacturing, distribution, use and end of life. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-carbon-footprint-vs-lca.html)

Creep

The slow, continuing deformation of a part under a load that stays on, such as a screw boss or a snap fit left bent. It matters most for plastics and is faster when they are warm, so use long-term (creep) modulus data for a sustained load. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/bracket-deflection-calculator.html)

Crimped terminal

A terminal fixed to the end of a wire by squeezing it on with dedicated crimp tooling. Harness suppliers have the tooling and test equipment to do this consistently, which is one reason to buy made-up harnesses. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cables-wiring-and-connectors-inside-a-product.html)

Critical to quality (CTQ)

A dimension, function or property that decides whether a product works, is safe or is acceptable to the customer. CTQ features are marked on drawings and checked more closely than the rest. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/planning-a-pilot-production-run.html)

Crowdfunding

Raising money from many people, often as pre-orders or rewards, before a product is made. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

Customer acquisition cost (CAC)

The average sales and marketing spend needed to win one new customer. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/investor-metrics-kpis.html)

Customer discovery

Talking to people who have a problem, about how they deal with it today, before designing a product to solve it. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/customer-discovery-for-hardware.html)

Customs value

The value on which import duty is calculated, usually the price paid plus transport and insurance to the UK border. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/landed-cost-freight-duty-vat.html)

Cutting die

A one-off tool, often called a cutter, that cuts and creases sheets of card into the shape of a particular box. Changing the box shape usually means a new cutter. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-ready-packaging-and-barcodes.html)

Cycle time

The time taken to make one shot or one part on a machine, a key driver of part cost. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

## D

Datum

A feature, such as a face, edge, hole or axis, that a drawing declares as the reference from which measurements start. Datums are usually the features that locate the part in an assembly. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/tolerances-and-engineering-drawings.html)

DDP

Delivered duty paid: an Incoterms rule under which the seller delivers to the buyer's premises with duty paid. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html)

Declaration of conformity

A signed statement by the manufacturer that a product meets the regulations that apply to it. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Deflection

How far a part moves when it bends under load, such as the drop at the tip of a bracket. For a simple beam it grows with the load and the cube of the length, and falls as the elastic modulus and second moment of area rise. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/bracket-deflection-calculator.html)

Descriptive mark

A name that simply describes a product or its qualities. Such names are generally hard to protect as trade marks, because other traders need to be free to use ordinary descriptive words; distinctive or invented names tend to be stronger. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/trade-marks-and-product-names.html)

Design for assembly (DFA)

Designing a product so it is quick and reliable to put together, for example with fewer parts and fasteners. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/assembly-time-estimate.html)

Design for manufacture (DFM)

Designing parts so they can be made reliably and economically by the chosen process. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Design freeze

The point at which a design is fixed and further changes go through change control. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/development-and-prototyping.html)

Design review

A short, structured meeting where the right people check a design against its requirements and risks, then decide whether it is ready to move to the next stage: proceed, proceed once named actions are closed, or rework. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/running-a-design-review.html)

Design right

In the UK, automatic protection against copying of the shape and configuration of a product. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/ip-partners-and-compliance.html)

Design verification

Testing production-intent parts against the requirements before committing to production. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/development-and-prototyping.html)

Designated standard

In Great Britain, a standard that gives a presumption of conformity with the relevant product regulations when it is met. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Development board

An off-the-shelf circuit board carrying a processor, radio or sensors with easy connections, used to prove electronics and firmware before a custom board is designed. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/electronics-in-a-physical-product.html)

Die casting

Forcing molten metal, often aluminium or zinc, into a steel die to make metal parts at volume. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/die-casting-explained.html)

Digital product passport

Product information on materials, repair and recycling that the EU plans to require for some product groups under its ecodesign framework. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/right-to-repair-and-ecodesign-rules.html)

Direct to consumer (DTC)

Selling directly to end customers, usually through your own website, without a retailer. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/route-to-market-and-margins.html)

Distributor

A business that buys products in bulk and sells them on to retailers or businesses, taking its own margin. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/route-to-market-and-margins.html)

Draft angle

The slight taper on faces parallel to the tool opening that lets a moulded part release cleanly. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Duty

A tax charged on imported goods, at a rate set by the product's commodity code and origin. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/landed-cost-freight-duty-vat.html)

## E

Ecodesign

Requirements for the environmental performance of products, such as energy-related products, over their life. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sustainability-and-product-life.html)

Effectivity

The point from which a change applies, given as a date, a production batch or a serial number. Recording it means you can always tell which units contain the old part and which contain the new one. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/bills-of-materials-and-revision-control.html)

Ejector pin

A pin in an injection-mould tool that pushes the finished part out; it leaves a small mark. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Elastic modulus

A material's stiffness, written E and given in MPa on its datasheet; also called Young's modulus. With the second moment of area it sets how far a part bends, and for plastics under a load that stays on, the long-term (creep) modulus applies. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/bracket-deflection-calculator.html)

Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC)

The ability of electrical equipment to work without causing or suffering unacceptable electromagnetic interference. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Embodied carbon

The greenhouse gas emissions from making a product's materials and parts, before it is used. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/carbon-footprint.html)

End cap

A plate or cap that closes an open end of an extruded enclosure and carries its connectors, lights and seal, usually screwed into the screw ports with a gasket against the cut end. Machined aluminium end plates suit low volumes; moulded plastic caps need a mould, so they usually come later. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/aluminium-extrusions-for-product-enclosures.html)

Engineering BOM (EBOM)

The bill of materials for the product as designed. It usually mirrors the assembly structure in the CAD model and is owned by the design team. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/bills-of-materials-and-revision-control.html)

Engineering change request (ECR)

A short, numbered record of a proposed change to a released part: what should change, why, and which part numbers are affected. It then carries the impact check, the approval decision and the effectivity, so the whole history of the change is in one place. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/change-request-builder.html)

Engineering prototype

A prototype that integrates form and function to check the design against its specification. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/development-and-prototyping.html)

Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS)

A UK scheme offering tax reliefs to investors in qualifying smaller companies. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

Equity

Ownership in a company; equity funding means selling shares in exchange for investment. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

Ergonomics

Designing a product to fit the people who use it: grip, reach, weight, balance, forces and comfort across the range of intended users. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/industrial-design-vs-engineering-design.html)

Evidence ladder

A way of ranking market evidence from weak (opinions) to strong (payments and commitments). [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/opportunity-and-concept.html)

EVT, DVT and PVT

Engineering, design and production validation testing: the last three development stages, as named in many electronics teams. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/development-and-prototyping.html)

Extended producer responsibility (EPR)

Rules that make producers responsible for the cost of managing their products or packaging at end of life. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sustainability-and-product-life.html)

Extrusion

A process that pushes material through a shaped die to make long parts with a constant cross-section, cut to length. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/aluminium-extrusions-for-product-enclosures.html)

Extrusion die

The steel disc, with the profile's shape cut through it, that heated aluminium is pushed through to make an extrusion. It is relatively simple, so it usually costs much less than a die-casting die or injection mould for a similar part, though cost rises with profile size, complexity and the number of hollows. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/aluminium-extrusions-for-product-enclosures.html)

EXW

Ex works: an Incoterms rule under which the buyer takes responsibility for the goods from the seller's premises. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html)

## F

Face seal

An O-ring seal in which the ring sits in a groove in a flat face and is squeezed as the two faces are pulled together, usually by screws. It depends on the faces closing fully and evenly. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

Failure mode

The way in which a product or part fails, such as cracking, wearing, leaking or not switching on. Recording failures by mode makes patterns and their causes easier to spot. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/after-launch-returns-feedback-and-design-changes.html)

Family tool

An injection-mould tool that makes several different parts in one cycle. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

FDM

Fused deposition modelling: 3D printing by extruding melted plastic filament layer by layer. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-a-3d-printing-process.html)

Field trial

Putting a small batch of products into real use to learn how they perform over time. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/development-and-prototyping.html)

Financial model

A spreadsheet that links unit cost, price, volume, fixed costs and payment timing to show profit, break-even and how much funding a business needs. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/building-a-hardware-financial-model.html)

Finite element analysis (FEA)

Computer simulation of stresses, deflections or heat in a design, used to check it before building.

Firm order

An order that commits the buyer to pay, as distinct from a forecast, which only helps the supplier plan. A supply agreement can say when orders become firm and whether the buyer pays for materials bought against a forecast. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/supply-agreements-with-a-manufacturer.html)

Firmware

The software built into a product's electronics that controls how the hardware behaves. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/estimating-hardware-development-costs.html)

First article inspection

A detailed check of the first production parts against the drawings to confirm the process is right. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/quality-control-and-first-article-inspection.html)

Fixed costs

Costs that do not change with the number of units sold, such as tooling, design and overheads. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/break-even-calculator.html)

Fixture (jig)

A holder that locates parts in the right position while they are assembled, glued, pressed or tested, so the operator no longer judges alignment by eye. A part that will not sit in its fixture is probably wrong or the wrong way round. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/assembly-and-work-instructions.html)

Flash

Thin fins of plastic along the parting line or around inserts and ejectors of a moulded part, usually caused by too much pressure or tool steel that does not seal. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/mould-tool-trials-and-sample-approval.html)

Flexible printed circuit (FPC)

A thin, flat, flexible circuit that links boards at different angles or on moving parts, and is the same in every unit. It needs a defined bend shape with no sharp creases, and care at assembly because its connectors are small and easy to fit at an angle. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cables-wiring-and-connectors-inside-a-product.html)

FOB

Free on board: an Incoterms rule under which the seller pays to load the goods onto the ship at the origin port. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html)

Food contact materials

Materials and parts intended to touch food or drink, such as containers, utensils and appliance parts. They need grades and evidence suited to that use, so check the rules early. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

Form, fit and function

The usual test of whether a changed part is interchangeable with the old one. If it can still replace the old part everywhere it is used without any other change, it gets a new revision; if not, it gets a new part number. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/bills-of-materials-and-revision-control.html)

Form-in-place gasket

A gasket made by dispensing a bead of liquid onto a flange by machine, which cures into a soft seal on the part. It follows complex shapes, but needs dispensing equipment and a groove or stop to set the compression. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

Freedom to operate

Whether a product can be made and sold without infringing other people's patents or rights. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/freedom-to-operate-explained.html)

Fulfilment

Storing, picking, packing and delivering orders to customers, done yourself or by a third party such as a marketplace. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/selling-on-marketplaces.html)

Functional unit

The basis a footprint or LCA compares on, such as one year of use, so products with different lifetimes compare fairly. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-carbon-footprint-vs-lca.html)

## G

Galvanic corrosion

Corrosion that happens when two different metals touch and are bridged by water, particularly salt water: the less noble metal, such as aluminium or zinc, corrodes faster. Using one metal throughout, or insulating the joint and keeping water out, prevents it. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-metals-for-a-product.html)

Gasket

A soft rubber or foam seal squeezed between two parts so it fills the small gaps between them. It needs a stiff flange and even, controlled compression to seal reliably. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

Gate

The point where plastic enters the cavity of an injection-mould tool; it leaves a small mark. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

General tolerance

The tolerance that applies to every dimension on a drawing that has none of its own, usually stated in the title block or by reference to a standard such as ISO 2768. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/tolerances-and-engineering-drawings.html)

Geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T)

A system of drawing symbols that controls the shape, orientation and location of features, such as the flatness of a face or the position of a hole, measured from datums. It complements plus-or-minus size tolerances. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/tolerances-and-engineering-drawings.html)

Golden sample

An approved reference unit that production parts are compared against. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html)

Grommet

A fitting in a hole through a wall that protects a cable from the edge of the hole. Where the product must be sealed, a cable gland or a sealed connector keeps water out. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cables-wiring-and-connectors-inside-a-product.html)

Gross margin

Revenue minus the cost of goods sold, often expressed as a percentage of revenue. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/route-to-market-and-margins.html)

GS1

The organisation that runs the barcode numbering system retailers commonly use. A business obtains its GTINs through membership of GS1 in its own country; in the UK that is GS1 UK. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-ready-packaging-and-barcodes.html)

GTIN

Global Trade Item Number: the number behind a retail barcode, identifying one specific product to tills and stock systems. Each variant a shopper could buy needs its own. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-ready-packaging-and-barcodes.html)

Gusset

A triangular rib that supports a boss or wall in a moulded part. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

## H

Hang tab

A tab with a hole or slot at the top of a retail pack so it can hang from a peg or hook in a shop. It must be strong enough for handling and let the pack hang straight. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-ready-packaging-and-barcodes.html)

Hardened steel tool

An injection-mould tool made from hardened steel for long life and high volumes. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Heat checking

Fine surface cracks that form on a die-casting die as every shot heats it sharply and it cools again. They show as raised lines on castings until the die is repaired. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/die-casting-explained.html)

Heat sink

Finned metal, usually aluminium, fixed to a hot component to give it more surface area to lose heat. It needs moving air around it, so it suits vented products better than small sealed ones. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/managing-heat-in-a-product-enclosure.html)

Heat-set insert

A threaded metal insert, usually brass, pressed into a hole in a plastic part with a heated tip, so the melted plastic flows into its knurls and holds it. It gives a thread that survives repeated assembly. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html)

Hollow and semi-hollow profiles

A hollow profile fully encloses at least one space, like a tube, so its die needs a mandrel supported on bridges; a solid profile, like a flat bar, encloses none. A semi-hollow profile nearly encloses a space through a narrow gap, like a C-shaped screw port, and can be harder to make than it looks because the thin tongue of die steel forming the gap is weak. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/aluminium-extrusions-for-product-enclosures.html)

Hot runner

A heated channel system in a mould that keeps plastic molten up to the cavity, reducing waste and sometimes cycle time. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Hot-chamber machine

A die-casting machine whose injection mechanism sits in the molten metal, so a plunger pushes each shot straight into the die and cycles are short. It is usually used for zinc and other low-melting alloys, and some magnesium. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/die-casting-explained.html)

## I

Import VAT

VAT charged on imported goods, normally reclaimable by VAT-registered businesses. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/landed-cost-freight-duty-vat.html)

Impregnation

A treatment that seals the porosity in a casting so it cannot leak. For die-cast parts that must seal, ask the die caster about it alongside leak testing. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/die-casting-explained.html)

In-mould decoration

Placing a printed film in an injection-mould tool so it is moulded into the part, giving graphics that do not wear off. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Inclusive design

Designing a product so it can be used by people with a wide range of abilities, ages and circumstances. Designing for the edges of the user group often makes a product easier for everyone. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/usability-testing-a-prototype.html)

Incoterms

International rules, published by the International Chamber of Commerce, that define who pays for transport, insurance and duty in a sale. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html)

Indented BOM

A bill of materials laid out in levels, with parts grouped under their sub-assemblies and quantities given per parent. It shows what a change touches, and a flat list of total quantities can be produced from it. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/bills-of-materials-and-revision-control.html)

Industrial design

Design focused on a product's form, use and appearance. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/industrial-design-vs-engineering-design.html)

Injection moulding

Making plastic parts by injecting molten plastic into a machined metal tool, cooling it and ejecting the part. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Inner pack

An optional level of packaging that groups a few unit packs together inside an outer case, to make handling and counting easier. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-ready-packaging-and-barcodes.html)

Innovate UK

The UK's innovation agency, which runs competitions for innovation funding. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

Insert

A part, often a threaded metal bush, placed into a plastic part by heat, ultrasound or moulding-in.

Intellectual property (IP)

Creations such as inventions, designs, brands and original written or drawn work that the law can protect, through patents, design rights, trade marks and copyright. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-protect-product-ip.html)

Interference fit

A fit in which the shaft is always larger than the hole, so the parts must be pressed or shrunk together. Used where parts must stay put without fasteners, such as bearings and dowels. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/tolerances-and-engineering-drawings.html)

Invest NI

Northern Ireland's economic development agency, which supports innovation and business growth. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

IP rating

Ingress protection rating: a code, such as IP54 or IP67, summarising how well an enclosure keeps out solids and water in standard tests. The first digit covers solid objects and dust, the second water; an X means that aspect was not tested. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

ISO 2768

An international standard for general tolerances, often quoted on drawings for dimensions that have no individual tolerance. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cnc-machining-design-rules.html)

## K

Keep-out zone

An area of a circuit board or enclosure where components, tracks or metal must not go, for example under a mounting boss or around an antenna. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/electronics-in-a-physical-product.html)

Key performance indicator (KPI)

A measure chosen to track progress towards a business goal, such as gross margin, sales growth or runway. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/investor-metrics-kpis.html)

## L

Labyrinth

Overlapping walls that force water to take a winding path into a housing, keeping out splashes and rain without a seal. It does not wear out, but will not stop water under pressure or immersion. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

Landed cost

The total cost of getting a product from the supplier to your warehouse ready to sell. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/landed-cost-calculator.html)

Layer lines

The visible ridges left on a 3D-printed part where each layer was built on the one below. They affect the look and feel of the part and, in FDM, where it is weakest. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-a-3d-printing-process.html)

Lead time

The time between placing an order and receiving the goods. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Lead-in angle

The sloping face of a snap-fit hook that rides over the catch as the parts are pushed together, also called the assembly angle. A shallower slope makes assembly easier but needs a longer hook. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-snap-fits-and-living-hinges.html)

Life cycle assessment (LCA)

A standard method for assessing a product's environmental impacts across its whole life. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-carbon-footprint-vs-lca.html)

Lifetime value (LTV)

The gross profit a business expects from a customer over the whole relationship, including repeat purchases, consumables and accessories. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/hardware-investor-metrics.html)

Lifter

A moving part in an injection-mould tool that releases an internal undercut as the part is ejected. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Light pipe

A clear plastic part that carries light from an LED on a circuit board to the outside of an enclosure. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/electronics-in-a-physical-product.html)

Limit sample

A part kept to show the worst acceptable version of a cosmetic feature, such as the largest acceptable gate mark. Production parts are compared with it, so cosmetic decisions do not depend on memory or opinion. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/mould-tool-trials-and-sample-approval.html)

Living hinge

A thin, flexible section of plastic that acts as a hinge, typically moulded in polypropylene. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-snap-fits-and-living-hinges.html)

Looks-like prototype

A model that shows a product's size, shape and appearance, but may not work. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/development-and-prototyping.html)

## M

Manufacturing BOM (MBOM)

The bill of materials for the product as built, grouped by how the factory assembles it. It adds things CAD does not show, such as glue, grease, protective film and packing materials. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/bills-of-materials-and-revision-control.html)

Marketplace

An online platform where third parties sell to consumers in exchange for commission and fees. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/route-to-market-and-margins.html)

Markup

Profit as a share of cost: (price minus cost) divided by cost. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-and-distributor-margins-explained.html)

Masking

Covering areas of a part, such as threads, fits and earthing points, so a coating, plating or anodising does not reach them. Masked areas should be few, simple and shown on the drawing. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Masterbatch

A concentrated mix of pigment or additive in a carrier plastic, blended with natural plastic at the moulding machine to colour or modify the part. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Match funding

A requirement that a grant recipient contributes part of the project cost from its own funds. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

Material certificate

A document from a material supplier confirming the grade, batch and key properties of the material supplied. It helps trace and check what went into a part. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/after-launch-returns-feedback-and-design-changes.html)

Membrane switch

A flat switch panel bonded to the face of a product, usually under a printed overlay that carries the graphics on its back face. It seals the face in one piece and needs little tooling; metal domes can add a click. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-buttons-switches-and-controls.html)

Membrane vent

A small patch of microporous membrane on a sealed housing that lets air through but blocks liquid water, so the pressure changes as the housing heats and cools do not strain the seal. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

Minimum order quantity (MOQ)

The smallest order a supplier will accept. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/minimum-order-quantities-and-cash.html)

MJF

Multi Jet Fusion: 3D printing that fuses fine plastic powder, usually nylon, layer by layer, giving tough functional parts without support structures. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-a-3d-printing-process.html)

Mould tool

The machined metal tool that shapes parts in injection moulding or casting. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Mould-flow analysis

Simulation of how plastic fills a mould, used to predict problems such as short shots, weld lines and warping. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Moulded texture

A matt or patterned surface made by texturing the surface of the mould tool, so every part comes out with it. Textured faces usually need more draft than plain ones. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Moulder

A company that runs injection-moulding machines to make parts from a mould tool. It may also make the tool, or work with a separate toolmaker. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Multi-cavity tool

A mould tool that makes several identical parts per cycle, lowering cost per part at higher tool cost. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

## N

NDA

Non-disclosure agreement: a contract that keeps shared information confidential. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/nda-generator.html)

Net price

The price after VAT, discounts and channel deductions: what the business actually receives. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/hardware-revenue-margin-planning.html)

Nominal wall

The standard wall thickness a moulded part is designed around. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Nylon (PA)

Polyamide: a strong, tough engineering plastic that absorbs moisture, often glass-filled for stiffness. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

## O

O-ring

A moulded rubber ring that sits in a groove and seals when squeezed between two parts. Because the groove controls the squeeze, it is one of the most dependable seals, and standard sizes are widely available. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

ODM

Original design manufacturer: a company that designs and makes products, often adapting an existing design for a client. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html)

OEM

Original equipment manufacturer: a company whose products or parts are sold under another brand or built into another product.

Outer case

The shipping carton that holds a number of retail packs, usually with its own label and sometimes its own barcode. Retail stock usually moves in outer cases on pallets. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-ready-packaging-and-barcodes.html)

Overflow

A small pocket beside the cavity of a die-casting die that collects the first, coldest metal and some trapped air. It is trimmed off the casting with the runner and flash. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/die-casting-explained.html)

Overheads

Running costs that are not tied to individual units, such as salaries, rent and software. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/break-even-calculator.html)

Overmoulding

Moulding one material, often a soft TPE, over another part to add grip, seals or colour. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

## P

Pad printing

Printing that transfers ink from an etched plate to a part with a soft silicone pad, so logos and markings can be applied to curved or recessed surfaces. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Part consolidation

Combining two or more parts that never move relative to each other into one, removing a part, a joint and an assembly step. The new part may need a new or modified tool. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/reducing-the-cost-of-an-existing-product.html)

Part count

The number of separate parts in a product. Each one adds tooling or set-up, stock, handling and assembly time, so reducing it is a core aim of design for assembly. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/assembly-time-estimate.html)

Parting line

The line where the two halves of a mould meet; it can leave a visible mark on the part. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Passivation

A chemical treatment for stainless steel that removes surface contamination, such as iron from tools, so the steel's own corrosion resistance works as intended. It barely changes the look of the part. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Patent

A registered right that protects how a new invention works, for a limited time, in return for public disclosure. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-protect-product-ip.html)

Payback period

The time taken for cumulative returns to repay an investment. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/manufacturing-payoff.html)

Payment terms

The agreed timing and conditions of payment between buyer and seller, such as a deposit with the order and the balance before shipment, or payment a set number of days after invoice. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/minimum-order-quantities-and-cash.html)

PC/ABS

A blend of polycarbonate and ABS that balances toughness, heat resistance and surface finish. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

Permissible strain

The most strain a plastic can take in a flexing feature, such as a snap fit, without cracking or staying bent, taken from the material supplier's design data for the exact grade. Suppliers often give a lower figure for a joint opened many times than for one assembled once. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-snap-fits-and-living-hinges.html)

Pilot production

A small production run on the real process to prove it can make the product repeatably. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/planning-a-pilot-production-run.html)

Pin-out

The record of which wire runs from which pin to which at each connector, usually given as a table on the harness drawing. Every harness should be checked for continuity and correct pin-out in production. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cables-wiring-and-connectors-inside-a-product.html)

Plating

Depositing a thin layer of metal, such as zinc, nickel or chrome, onto a part for corrosion protection, wear resistance or a decorative metal look. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Poka-yoke (error-proofing)

A Japanese term for error-proofing: arranging the design, fixture or process so a mistake cannot be made, or is caught straight away. Asymmetric parts that only fit one way and keyed connectors are common examples. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/assembly-and-work-instructions.html)

Polycarbonate (PC)

A very tough, heat-resistant plastic available in transparent grades. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

Polypropylene (PP)

A light, tough, chemical-resistant plastic often used for containers and living hinges. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

Porosity

Small pores inside a casting, from trapped gas and from shrinkage where thick sections freeze last; every die casting has some. Machining can open pores into a leak path on a sealing face or weak engagement in a thread, so machined features are kept in even sections. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/die-casting-explained.html)

Potting

Filling the space around electronics with resin that sets solid. It protects well against water and vibration, but adds weight and makes the board unrepairable. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

Powder coating

A finish in which a dry powder is sprayed onto a metal part and baked into a tough, even coat. It comes in many colours and textures, builds up thicker than paint and is electrically insulating. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Pre-certified radio module

A ready-made radio module that has already been tested as a module. It reduces the radio testing a product needs, but it does not certify the whole product and its antenna guidance must still be followed. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/electronics-in-a-physical-product.html)

Pre-compliance testing

Informal testing during development to find compliance problems before formal certification tests. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Pre-order

An order and payment taken before a product is available, used to fund and test demand. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-validate-a-product-idea.html)

Pre-shipment inspection

A check of a sample from a finished, packed batch before it leaves the factory, against an agreed standard and sampling plan. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/quality-control-and-first-article-inspection.html)

Price break

A quantity at which a supplier's unit price steps down. Asking every supplier for the same price breaks makes their quotes comparable. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/comparing-manufacturing-quotes.html)

Printed circuit board (PCB)

The board that holds and connects a product's electronic components through copper tracks. Once the components are fitted it is often called a PCB assembly (PCBA). [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/estimating-hardware-development-costs.html)

Product liability

The legal responsibility of producers for harm caused by defective products. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-liability-basics.html)

Product requirements document (PRD)

A written list of what a product must do, for whom, with measurable targets and constraints. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/opportunity-and-concept.html)

Profile (extrusion)

The cross-section of an extrusion, and the lengths of aluminium made with it. An off-the-shelf enclosure profile needs no tooling; a custom profile needs its own die. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/aluminium-extrusions-for-product-enclosures.html)

Proof of principle

An early build that tests whether a product's core idea works. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/development-and-prototyping.html)

Prototype

An early version of a product built to answer a specific question about it. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/prototype-strategy-tool.html)

Pugh matrix

A concept-selection method that scores options against a reference design, criterion by criterion. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/pugh-concept-selector.html)

Purchase order

A formal order from a buyer to a supplier stating items, quantities, prices and terms. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/supply-agreements-with-a-manufacturer.html)

## Q

Quality plan

An agreed description of inspections, acceptance criteria and responsibilities for making a product. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html)

Quote validity

How long a supplier's quoted price holds, and the conditions, such as changes in material prices, under which it may be revised. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/comparing-manufacturing-quotes.html)

## R

R&D tax relief

UK Corporation Tax relief on qualifying research and development spending. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

Radial seal

An O-ring seal in which the ring sits around a plug or spigot and is squeezed against the wall of a bore as one part slides into the other. The fit sets the squeeze, which suits round lids and end caps. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sealing-and-waterproofing-an-enclosure.html)

Ramp-up

The period after a successful pilot run when production builds up from first batches to full volume, while any remaining actions are closed. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/planning-a-pilot-production-run.html)

Recycled content

The share of a product or material made from recycled sources. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/sustainability-and-product-life.html)

Registered design

A registered right protecting the appearance of a product. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/design-registration-vs-patents.html)

Registered trade mark (®)

A trade mark registered for particular goods and services in a particular country or region. The ® symbol indicates a registered mark and should only be used once it is registered, and only where it is registered; ™ can be used with a name you treat as a trade mark whether or not it is registered. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/trade-marks-and-product-names.html)

Request for quotation (RFQ)

A request to suppliers for a price, sent with drawings, quantities and requirements. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/how-to-find-and-brief-a-manufacturer.html)

Retail price (RRP)

Recommended retail price: the price the end customer is expected to pay, usually including VAT in the UK. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/hardware-revenue-margin-planning.html)

Retention angle

The face of a snap-fit hook that holds the parts together once assembled. At or near 90° to the pull the joint cannot be pulled apart; a shallower angle lets the hook slide out under a firm pull. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-snap-fits-and-living-hinges.html)

Revision

A recorded version of a part, drawing or bill of materials, usually marked with a letter such as Rev B. Each change raises the revision, so everyone can tell exactly which version they are working from. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/bills-of-materials-and-revision-control.html)

Rib

A thin wall added to a moulded part for stiffness without making the main wall thicker. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Right to repair

Rules and expectations that products can be repaired, for example through spare parts and repair information being available. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/right-to-repair-and-ecodesign-rules.html)

Risk assessment

A documented review of the hazards a product could present and how they are controlled. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

RoHS

Rules restricting certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Root cause analysis

Working back from a reported symptom to the underlying reason it happened, so the fix removes the cause rather than the symptom. A common method is to keep asking why, sometimes called the five whys. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/after-launch-returns-feedback-and-design-changes.html)

Root sum of squares (RSS)

A statistical way of combining tolerances in a stack-up that assumes each varies randomly and independently. It predicts the range most assemblies will fall in, which is narrower than a worst-case analysis. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/tolerance-stack-up.html)

Rotary encoder

A turning control that counts steps, often with detents you can feel, whereas a potentiometer gives a position. Its shaft needs a seal, and it should be held in the housing so side loads stay off the board. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-buttons-switches-and-controls.html)

Route to market

How a product reaches customers: direct, marketplaces, retailers, distributors or business sales. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/route-to-market-and-margins.html)

Rules of origin

Rules that decide where goods come from for trade purposes, which can affect duty under trade agreements. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/landed-cost-freight-duty-vat.html)

Runner

The channel in a mould that carries molten plastic from the sprue to the gates. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Runway

How long a business can operate before its cash runs out at the current burn rate. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/cashflow-projection.html)

## S

Safety factor

The allowable stress divided by the calculated stress: how much margin a part has. It is only as good as the allowable figure used; with the yield strength, a factor of 1 means the part is just starting to bend permanently. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/bracket-deflection-calculator.html)

Sale or return

A trade arrangement where a retailer can return unsold stock to the supplier, which keeps the stock risk. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-and-distributor-margins-explained.html)

Scrap rate

The share of parts or products rejected during manufacture. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/product-cost-estimator.html)

Screen printing

Printing that pushes ink through a fine mesh stencil onto a part, suited to flat or gently curved faces and larger areas of colour. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/surface-finishes-for-plastic-and-metal-parts.html)

Screw port

A channel built into an extruded profile, usually in the corners, that screws go straight into, so end caps can be fixed with no drilling or inserts. Agree its shape and size with the extruder and fastener supplier. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/aluminium-extrusions-for-product-enclosures.html)

Second moment of area

A property of a cross-section's shape and size, written I, that sets how well it resists bending; the material's elastic modulus sets the rest. For a flat bar it rises with the cube of the thickness, so doubling the thickness makes it eight times stiffer. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/bracket-deflection-calculator.html)

Second source

An alternative supplier or interchangeable part that can replace a component if the first becomes unavailable, so one shortage does not stop production. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/electronics-in-a-physical-product.html)

Seed Enterprise Investment Scheme (SEIS)

A UK scheme offering tax reliefs to investors in very early-stage qualifying companies. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/funding-and-cash.html)

Self-clinching fastener

A nut, stud or standoff pressed into a hole in sheet metal so that the metal flows into its grooves and locks it in place, giving a strong thread in sheet too thin to tap. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html)

Service loop

A little controlled slack left in a cable so a board can be lifted out and unplugged without straining it. It should be clipped so it cannot wander into a seam. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cables-wiring-and-connectors-inside-a-product.html)

Settlement discount

A small discount offered to a buyer for paying an invoice early. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-and-distributor-margins-explained.html)

Sheet metal

Parts made by cutting, punching and bending flat metal sheet, such as enclosures and brackets. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/manufacturing-and-cost.html)

Shelf-ready packaging

Outer cases designed to open into a display tray, so staff can put the whole case on the shelf without unpacking each unit. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/retail-ready-packaging-and-barcodes.html)

Short shot

A moulding defect in which the plastic does not fill the tool, leaving the part incomplete, often at the end furthest from the gate or at thin features. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/mould-tool-trials-and-sample-approval.html)

Shrinkage

The reduction in size as plastic cools in the mould; tools are cut oversize to allow for it. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

Side action

A moving part of a mould tool that forms an undercut and slides out before the part is ejected. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Silicone keypad

A moulded silicone rubber part carrying one or more buttons, with carbon pills underneath that press on contact pads on the circuit board. Clamped round its edge it is both button and seal, with a softer press than a tactile switch, but it needs its own mould. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-buttons-switches-and-controls.html)

Silicone tooling

Soft moulds made from silicone around a master pattern, used for vacuum casting short runs. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/prototyping-vs-production-startup-guide.html)

Sink mark

A shallow depression on a moulded surface caused by a thick section shrinking as it cools. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

SLA

Stereolithography: 3D printing that cures liquid resin with light, giving fine detail and smooth surfaces. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-a-3d-printing-process.html)

SLS

Selective laser sintering: 3D printing that fuses nylon powder with a laser, producing strong functional parts. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-a-3d-printing-process.html)

Snap fit

A moulded feature that clips parts together without separate fasteners. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-snap-fits-and-living-hinges.html)

Sprue

The main channel through which plastic enters a mould from the machine nozzle. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Staking

Fixing a part with a hole onto a plastic post by melting the tip of the post into a head, like a rivet, with a heated tool or ultrasonic vibration. Removing the part means cutting off the heads. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html)

Standard

A published document setting out agreed requirements or test methods, such as a British or European standard. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Steel-safe

Describes a mould feature first cut so that any likely correction only means removing steel, which is much easier than adding it back. A hole might be cut slightly small so it can be opened up after measuring. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/mould-tool-trials-and-sample-approval.html)

STEP file

A neutral 3D CAD file format that most CAD systems can open, commonly used to share part models with suppliers. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/must-have-documents-before-talking-to-a-manufacturer.html)

STL file

A common file format for 3D printing that describes a part's surface as a mesh of small triangles. It loses the exact geometry, so a STEP file is usually sent as well. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-a-3d-printing-process.html)

Straight pull

A moulded part or feature that can come straight out of a two-part mould tool as it opens, with no side actions or lifters. Straight-pull parts make simpler, cheaper tools. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/from-3d-printed-prototype-to-moulded-part.html)

Strain relief

A feature that takes the pull on a cable at the housing, so the force does not reach the connector or solder joints. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cables-wiring-and-connectors-inside-a-product.html)

Stress raiser (stress concentration)

A feature that concentrates stress, such as a sharp internal corner, the root of a boss or rib, a hole near an edge or a sudden change in wall thickness. Cracks tend to start there, so generous radii help. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-for-drops-and-impacts.html)

Supply agreement

A written agreement setting the rules for a whole relationship with a manufacturer: specification and quality, tooling, IP, pricing, orders, delivery, payment, changes, responsibility for faults and how the relationship ends. Each purchase order then only deals with quantities, dates and prices. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/supply-agreements-with-a-manufacturer.html)

Support structures

Temporary material printed under overhangs to hold them up while a part is 3D printed, then removed afterwards, usually leaving marks. Powder bed processes such as SLS and MJF do not need them. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-a-3d-printing-process.html)

Surface finish

The texture and appearance of a part's surface, such as as-machined, polished, textured, bead-blasted or painted. Finer or specified finishes usually add cost. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/cnc-machining-design-rules.html)

Surface preparation

Cleaning and treating a surface before bonding, painting or coating, for example by removing grease and mould release, abrading or priming, so the adhesive or coating holds. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html)

## T

T1 samples

The first samples from a new mould sent to the customer to check against the drawing, before the tool is modified. Labels vary: many toolmakers call the very first shots T0, so agree what each label means. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/mould-tool-trials-and-sample-approval.html)

Tactile switch

A small switch on the circuit board that gives a crisp click after a short travel, usually pressed by a plastic button in the housing. It is made to be pressed straight down, so the button needs an end stop and the board needs support under it. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/designing-buttons-switches-and-controls.html)

Target cost

The most a product can cost to make and land while still meeting the business's margin at its price and route to market. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/route-to-market-simulator.html)

Teardown

Taking apart a competitor's product to understand its parts, materials, manufacturing methods and likely cost. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/competitor-and-patent-landscape-review.html)

Technical file

The documentation that supports a product's conformity: design, risk assessment, standards and test reports. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Temper

The condition an alloy is supplied in, such as soft, hard or fully heat-treated. The same alloy's strength differs considerably between tempers, so specify the temper as well as the alloy. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/aluminium-extrusions-for-product-enclosures.html)

Test fixture

A purpose-made rig that holds a part or circuit board in a repeatable position for testing or programming, often touching test points with spring-loaded pins. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/electronics-in-a-physical-product.html)

Test point

A pad or contact on a circuit board placed so that a fixture or probe can reach power, programming or key signals during testing and production. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/electronics-in-a-physical-product.html)

Thermal pad

A soft, heat-conducting pad that fills the gap between a warm component and a heatsink or case wall, giving the heat a path out. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/managing-heat-in-a-product-enclosure.html)

Thermal resistance

How strongly a heat path resists the flow of heat, in degrees Celsius per watt (°C/W): how many degrees warmer one end gets for each watt flowing through it. Resistances in a chain add, and the temperature rise is the power multiplied by the total. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/temperature-rise-estimator.html)

Thermoforming

Heating plastic sheet and forming it over a mould, used for trays, covers and large thin parts. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/manufacturing-and-cost.html)

Think-aloud

A usability testing method in which participants say what they are looking for, expecting and noticing as they work through tasks, so observers can see why they hesitate or make mistakes. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/usability-testing-a-prototype.html)

Thread-forming screw

A screw designed to form its own thread in a plain hole in a plastic part, with no insert or tapping. The thread wears each time it is removed, so it suits joints opened occasionally. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html)

Title block

The box of information in the corner of an engineering drawing, giving details such as the part name and number, revision, material, scale and general tolerance. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/tolerances-and-engineering-drawings.html)

Tolerance

The permitted variation in a dimension. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Tolerance band

The total range a dimension may vary within, from its lower limit to its upper limit. How the bands of two mating parts sit relative to each other decides the fit. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/tolerances-and-engineering-drawings.html)

Tolerance stack-up

The combined effect of tolerances on several parts on a fit or gap in an assembly.

Tool transfer

Moving a production tool, such as a mould, out of a supplier's factory to the owner or another supplier. Agreeing in advance how it can be collected, how much notice is needed and whether any costs apply, such as packing or outstanding invoices, keeps that route open. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/supply-agreements-with-a-manufacturer.html)

Tooling

The moulds, dies, jigs and fixtures needed to make parts in production. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

Tooling ownership

Who owns a production tool such as a mould, and so whether it can be moved to another supplier. It should be agreed in writing, with who pays for repairs and changes. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/comparing-manufacturing-quotes.html)

Toolmaker

The company or specialist that designs and makes mould tools, and reviews part designs for mouldability before the tool is cut. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-explained.html)

TPE

Thermoplastic elastomer: a rubber-like plastic that can be moulded and over-moulded. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/choosing-plastic-materials.html)

Traceability

Being able to identify where and when a product or batch was made, and from which materials. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/product-certification-basics.html)

Trade mark

A sign, such as a product or brand name or a logo, that tells customers whose product they are buying. It protects the brand, not the product's design or how it works; registration generally makes the rights clearer and easier to enforce. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/trade-marks-and-product-names.html)

Trade mark attorney

A professional adviser who specialises in trade marks, including searches, applications and dealing with objections. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/trade-marks-and-product-names.html)

Transit testing

Repeatable drop, vibration and compression tests that check packaging protects a product in shipping. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/packaging-design-for-shipping.html)

Transition fit

A fit in which the hole and shaft tolerances overlap, so some pairs have a small gap and some a slight press. Used for accurate location where parts still need to come apart. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/tolerances-and-engineering-drawings.html)

Trim tool

A press tool that removes the runner, overflows and flash from die castings at volume. It is a separate cost from the die, so check it is in the quote. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/die-casting-explained.html)

## U

UK Trade Tariff

Ultrasonic welding

Joining two plastic parts by pressing them together and vibrating them at high frequency until the interface melts and fuses. The joint is quick, strong and can seal, but cannot be undone. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html)

Undercut

A feature that stops a moulded part being pulled straight out of the tool. [More](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/injection-moulding-dfm-checklist.html)

Title: Assembly Time Estimator

Live tool

Built by [Andrew Hunter](https://oriondesign.xyz/about/), Product Design Engineer · Free to use · Method and assumptions

# Assembly Time Estimator

Estimate manual assembly time during concept development. Use it to compare architectures, part-count changes,
fastening strategies, and labour-rate sensitivity before detailed process planning exists.

## Worked example

A 12-part product with 8 joins, moderate handling, and 20 seconds of QA time often lands near the point where small part-count reductions
create meaningful labour savings. Removing two joins and one orientation step can cut recurring assembly effort more than teams expect.

## How to use the estimate

This tool is most useful when comparing concepts, not validating final takt time. If one direction uses fewer components,
easier location features, or less repeated fastening, the delta in labour usually matters more than the absolute number.

- Use part count as a proxy for handling events.

- Treat joins as repeated manual effort that scales directly with labour cost.

- Use reorientation count to capture awkward fixture or operator movement.

- Add QA time to reflect inspection and confirmation effort that often gets forgotten.

## Method and assumptions

Handling time = part count × seconds per part (7 simple, 12 moderate, 18 complex)
Joining time = fasteners × seconds per fastener
Reorientation time = reorientations × 6 seconds
Total seconds = handling + joining + reorientation + inspection
Labour cost per unit = total seconds ÷ 3,600 × hourly labour rate

**Assumptions**

- Handling times per part are fixed allowances for manual assembly by a trained operator, chosen by the complexity setting.

- Each reorientation of the assembly takes about 6 seconds.

- The labour rate is the fully loaded rate you enter.

**Limits**

- It does not include learning curves, fixtures, line balancing, rework or automation.

- Real times depend on part design, access, tooling and operator skill; time a prototype build to calibrate.

## How to read your result

The first figure is the estimated hands-on time to build one unit. The second turns that into labour cost per unit at your
chosen rate, and the third shows what that adds up to across the batch. The chart shows where the time goes, which is usually
more useful than the total itself.

- **Comfortable:** simple handheld or housewares products typically land at around one to three minutes. If yours does, assembly is unlikely to be your main cost problem.

- **Worth a look:** small electromechanical products with wiring, a [PCB](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/electronics-in-a-physical-product.html) and several fastened joints often sit somewhere between three and ten minutes. Check whether joining or reorientation dominates the chart, because those are the easiest to design out.

- **Worrying:** if labour cost per unit is a large share of your target unit cost, or one slice of the chart is far bigger than the others, the design probably needs simplifying before tooling is committed.

Common next steps are combining parts, swapping screws for [snap fits](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/joining-methods-for-product-design.html) or self-locating features, and arranging the build so
everything goes in from one direction. Re-run the estimate after each change to see which one moves the number most.
Save your result to your [product plan](https://oriondesign.xyz/tools/product-plan-builder.html) so the labour assumption sits alongside your
cost and pricing work. If the estimate is high and the fix is not obvious, a short [conversation with Andrew](https://oriondesign.xyz/contact/)
can help you see where the design could be simplified.

Related reading

[Estimating Assembly Time During Design](https://oriondesign.xyz/guides/assembly-time-estimate.html)
